verdicts.reason: Numbers and duties match the section. Hook thresholds lack 'more than' and the idle-crane intervals are loose, but nothing is wrong or invented.
Accurate operator summary. Load handling, limit-switch trials, inspection intervals, idle and standby requirements, lockout steps and numeric limits all match the source.
Accurate inspector checklist. Modifications, clearances, bumpers, brakes, voltages, rope wraps, test loads, inspections, maintenance and extinguisher ban all match the source.

Scope, operators, design dates, the rating table, the 110% test limit, the ±10% weight rule, inspection intervals and handling rules all match the source. The cut-down summary leaves no central limit out.
Numbers and duties match: the table and footnote, the 1% grade, idle and standby inspections, certifications, rope approval, the maintenance rule and outrigger use. Nothing is added.

Correctly covers the locomotive stipulations, SAE J765, testing and rerating, idle and standby cross-references, certification contents, the 'should' wording and the cross-references to other sections. No errors found.

No factual errors, but it entirely leaves out central duties and limits: chain proof testing before use (e)(4), the mesh temperature ranges (g)(7), the fiber-rope temperature range and splice tuck minimums (h)(2)-(3), and the wire-rope broken-wire and wear thresholds (f)(5). Saying mesh is tested 'at 1 1/2 times' also drops the word 'minimum'.

Accurate summary. The numbers match the source: 12 months, 1000/600 °F, the table entry, 15%/10°, 10/40/96, 200/400/-60 °F, the wire-rope removal thresholds, mesh ranges and limits, fiber tucks and angle, and the web temperatures and proof tests. It adds nothing the section lacks.

Thorough and accurate for an inspector. It correctly covers records, certificates, the A391-65 reference, the welding exception, the fiber tail rules, mesh coating timing, and the web repair rules. It adds nothing the section lacks.
Accurate plain-language summary of coverage, attachments, key exclusions, knuckle-boom limits and employer work-rule duty; no added content.
Accurate on exclusions, digger derrick conditions, and knuckle-boom delivery conditions. Forklift exception slightly shortened but not wrong.
Faithful inspector checklist covering (c)(4), (c)(18), (e), (g), (h). Some exclusions are summarized vaguely but nothing is wrong.
Matches the source on competent person, qualified person, A/D director, fall zone, two blocking, encroachment, dedicated spotter, load, rated capacity and 'up to'. Nothing is added.

Accurate on the load moment indicator and limiter, boom hoist limiting device, range control devices, controlled lowering versus free fall, dedicated channel, tower crane terms and multi-purpose machine coverage.

Accurate on coverage, roles, evaluators, NRTL listing, encroachment, runway, travel bogie and the interpretive terms. The 'Paragraph'/'Section' sentence is awkward but correct, since both apply 'unless otherwise specified'.
Accurate trainee summary of (a)-(c), (e), (f). Leaving out (d), the fallback when there is no controlling entity, is a gap but not a central duty, and it makes no statement wrong.
Faithful, covers every paragraph including (d), and adds nothing. The simpler wording of the 'ground conditions' definition is acceptable.
Precise and faithful. Correctly limits (d) to (c)(1) and states the railroad exclusion conditions exactly.
Gets right the prohibitions duty, the choice between (a) and (b), the § 1926.1406 condition and the synthetic-sling note. Adds nothing and fits the trainee level.
Correctly separates the fixed prohibitions duty from the choice of procedures. The quotes and cross-references are right, and it says the cross-referenced content is not given here.

Reads the structure correctly, including the 'and' that ties the prohibitions duty to the choice and the employer's burden to demonstrate. It does not make up what § 1926.1406 or § 1926.1404(r) require.

Accurate plain-language summary for trainees. Covers the A/D director, crew instructions, out-of-view protection, the pin-removal exception, capacity, hazards, cantilever limits, weights, configuration, shipping pins, pile driving, outriggers and rigging. Leaving out the engineer fallback is acceptable for a summary, and the outrigger gloss is harmless.
Faithful at operator level. States the brake test, the locomotive crane exception for wheel unloading, the engineer fallbacks and the rigging duties correctly, with nothing invented.

Correct inspector checklist. Cross-references (1926.1402, 1417(o)(3), 1434, 1412(c), 1926.251(c)(9)) are accurate. Wheel unloading correctly excludes stabilizers and locomotive cranes, and the locomotive crane procedures are stated correctly.
Accurately states scope, the partly/completely point and all four pin restrictions (a)-(d); plain language suits a trainee; nothing added.
Faithful to (a)-(d), correctly notes (d) covers top pins only; the opening framing restates the section's structure and is not a new duty.
Correctly matches each pin location to its support condition; claims of no numbers, no exceptions, no bottom pins in (d) and no cited standards are all true.
Correctly states the trigger, all three conditions and the qualified-person requirement. The plain wording suits a trainee, and nothing is added.
Accurate, with correct scope wording ('any part', 'all parts', 'part or all'). It rightly says the section has no definition of a qualified person and no numeric limits.

Correct trigger, checklist items and authorship requirement. It accurately notes the 'dangerous' wording difference between (a)(1) and (a)(3), and that the section has no exceptions, numbers or definitions.

It leaves out paragraph (e) completely, which is the utility's duty to give requested voltage information within two working days. That is a numeric limit of the section. It also says only that warnings go 'on the equipment', with no cab or exterior counts.

It is accurate and covers all options, the two-day voltage rule, the (b) measures, the (c)/(d) bans, the energized presumption and the warning postings. It fits the operator level. 'Plus two outside' is a small loss of 'at least' but is not wrong.

It is accurate and complete for an inspector: it lists all spotter elements, the alternative measures, the (c)/(d) conditions, the 'has been and continues to be' wording, and the warning counts with the exception.

Accurately covers the work zone, the 20-ft trigger, the three options, all Table A values, the two-day voltage rule, paragraph (b) precautions with the subpart V exception, below-line work, the energized presumption and training. Leaving out (f) and (h) is acceptable for a summary.

Faithful and detailed: correct options, Table A, the (b) measures including the rule for when the operator can't see the warning line, spotter duties, the subpart V exception, transmitter precautions, training and manufacturer conditions. No invented content.

Accurate inspector checklist: options, Table A, (b)(3)/(b)(4)/(b)(5), below-line exceptions including the boom conditions and § 1926.1410, training under § 1926.1430(g), and (h). Omitting 'if used' for tag lines is minor in checklist form.
Accurately states the cross-reference to 1407/1408, the 20→50 ft substitution for lines at or below 1000 kV, and who sets the distance above 1000 kV. Adds nothing and suits a trainee.
Accurate. The points about exactly 1000 kV and the 'wherever' wording follow from the text, and it correctly notes no method is given. Suits an operator.

Accurate summary covering the prohibition, both infeasibility findings, clearance setting, key procedures, the substitute deadlines, the 10-foot barricade, documentation, the director, stoppage and training. Nothing is invented. Shortening the (j) alternatives doesn't make any statement wrong.

Faithful operator-level coverage of (a) through (m), including the subpart V exceptions, the dates, the 10-foot limit, the (j) options for resuming work and the manufacturer conditions in (k). Nothing is added.

Accurate inspector checklist. The clearance factors, the substitute conditions and dates, the 10-foot barricade, the § 1926.1415 reference and § 1926.1408(g) training are all correct, and nothing is invented.

Scope, lowering, clearances, speed/terrain, Table T values, 20-ft spotter trigger and poor-visibility measures are all accurate. Leaving out the spotter's sub-duties is acceptable for a trainee summary.
Accurate and complete: correct cross-references, Table T values, spotter duties and night measures, with nothing added.
Accurate and complete, with precise sub-paragraph citations. Correctly notes that the (b)(1)-(4) measures still apply in poor visibility.

It accurately summarizes the shift, monthly, annual, modification/repair/assembly, severe service, idle and manufacturer requirements. The numbers are right (3 months, 12 months, 3 months idle) and nothing is invented.

It is accurate and faithful at operator level. It covers the shift items, the disassembly/boom-down condition, the FRA exceptions, the deficiency actions, monthly records, the annual exception and monitoring, severe service, idle equipment and manufacturer procedures, with correct retention periods.

It is an accurate inspector checklist. It covers the §1926.1434 approval, criteria and RPE development (including 'familiar with the equipment type' for assembly), use restrictions, documentation details, the (f)(4)-(6) actions with the 1416(d)/1435(e) exceptions, severe service, idle equipment, (j), and document availability under (k).

Accurate trainee summary. Category limits, 5%, two drum wraps, splice ban, power-line rule, tag-out, documentation and lubricant ban all match the source. Leaving out the details of the annual inspection is acceptable for a summary.

Accurate operator summary of the shift, category, monthly and annual duties. All numbers are correct, including the manufacturer's written-approval alternative and the severing limits. It adds nothing the section lacks.

Accurate and thorough inspector checklist. It correctly covers the arc-damage wording, all Category II limits, the energized-line repair ban, the 6-month and disassembly exception, documentation cross-references and document access.

Accurate summary at trainee level. The design factors (3.5 floor, 5 standard), the Type I written-approval exception, the Types II/III limits, the boom hoist limits, and the socketing and seizing rules all match the source. Leaving out the rated-capacity wording in option (2) is an acceptable simplification.

Faithful to the source. It correctly covers the per-lift rules in (e)(3), the boom hoist conditions including the 18x pitch diameters and the design factor of five, and the clip, socketing and seizing rules. Nothing is added.

A detailed checklist at inspector level that matches the source. It correctly covers the type definitions, the design factor rules, the (e)(3) checks and each boom hoist sub-requirement (A)-(G), including the 18-for-16 substitution and how the design factor is calculated.

Accurate trainee summary. The indicator exclusions and the general mention of exceptions are correct, and all of (b) is stated faithfully. It leaves out the tag-out/removal detail and the cross-reference, but neither is central and nothing becomes wrong.
Complete and accurate for operators. Every device, exception, tag-out/removal rule and (b) duty matches the source, and no requirement is added.
Accurate inspector checklist. Exclusions, exceptions, malfunction handling, (b) duties and the cross-reference all match the source.
Accurate trainee summary: repair limits, parts exceptions, dates, 6,000 lb threshold and the stop-work duty all match the source; nothing added.
Fallbacks, dates and repair limits match the source. Minor: 'apply only to digger derricks' drops 'those' from (a)(2), but the rest of the item shows it is not misapplying the rule.
Detailed and faithful: both repair exceptions, the §1926.1417(j) cross-reference, the marine exception quote and all alternatives are correct. Same minor 'only digger derricks' wording as item 1.

Accurate trainee-level summary. The key numbers (75 percent trigger, 90% line pull, two full wraps) and central duties are right, with nothing invented. Calling the working gear 'lightweight' simplifies the 'negligible weight relative to capacity' condition but doesn't distort it.

Correctly covers the conditions for leaving a suspended load, the response to warning signs, both load-weight methods, the brake test, two wraps, and the front-lift exception for wheel-mounted equipment. Leaving out storm warnings and employer shift notices is acceptable for an operator-level summary.

Detailed and faithful inspector checklist. It covers the qualified-person and professional-engineer split, the fall-zone exclusion with its cross-references, the working-gear exception, travel requirements, locomotive cranes, and the tower-crane counterweight cross-reference. No errors.

Correctly states the trigger, the authority to stop and to refuse loads, and the end point (a qualified person determines safety is assured). It rightly notes the term is not defined and there are no numbers. Nothing is added.
Accurate and suited to an operator. The quotes are exact, and the statements about what the section leaves out (definition, method, time limit, notification) are all true.

Breaks the sentence down correctly into condition, authority and duration. The compliance points come straight from the text, and the claims about missing exceptions, cross-references and documentation are correct.
Accurate trainee-level summary. It omits the (g) condition for resuming and the (m)(2) alternative, but neither omission makes a statement wrong.
Faithful operator-level summary covering all duties, the (j) exception, the §1926.1417(y) note and both (m) options.
Accurate and complete inspector checklist that quotes (d) correctly and adds no content.
It covers the on-site test before operations, the dedicated channel with both exceptions, and hands-free reception, all accurately. The opening sentence about the lift is framing, not a new duty.
It is faithful to (a), (b)(1), (b)(2) and (c). The quotes are correct and it adds nothing.
It is accurate. Saying the section has no test method or recordkeeping requirement is correct, and reading 'and' in (b)(2) as requiring both conditions follows the text.
It covers paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) accurately. The three elements are read correctly from the semicolons, and nothing is added.
It is accurate and addressed to the operator. Saying 'etc.' means the examples aren't a complete list is a fair reading of the text.

It is accurate and fits the inspector level. The 'verify' and 'check' points follow directly from the text, and the statements that no language is specified and no other standards are cited are correct.
Accurate trainee-level summary; scope, walkway dimensions, 6/15 ft thresholds, and load-line conditions correct; exceptions described vaguely but not wrongly.
Accurate: walkway rules, (e)/(f)/(h) triggers and exceptions, anchorage tests, load-line conditions and training all match the section.
Precise scope mapping, correct standards, crawler-tread exception, notes no exceptions for erecting/climbing/dismantling; all faithful.

Accurate on applicability, training, barriers and exception, and notifying the operator. It omits the operator's no-rotation duty (a)(3)(ii) and who sets up the (b) system, both reasonable to leave out at trainee level.
Faithful to (a)(1)-(a)(3) and (b). 'Authorized personnel', the exception and the pre-arranged communication rule are correct. Not naming who institutes the (b) system is acceptable for operators.
Accurate and complete, including the exception's demonstration requirement and who is responsible for coordination when there is no controlling entity.
Accurate summary of (a)-(e) for trainees. Leaving out the definition of 'essential' and the free-fall note makes nothing wrong.
Accurate and complete, including the essential-employee test, the infeasibility showing and the free-fall note. Fits the operator level.
Faithful inspector checklist covering all paragraphs, the examples and the cross-reference to §1926.1426.

Accurately covers the (a)(1) bans, the (a)(2) conditions for permitted use, the backup requirement in (b), retraction protection in (c) and the load line rules in (d). It correctly gives the shaft ban in (d) no exception. Leaving out the drum details is acceptable for a trainee summary.

Faithful to the section, including the power line area and travel-radius condition, the shaft and cofferdam exceptions, the friction and hydraulic drum requirements, the rule that clutches and hydraulic motors don't count as brakes, and the controlled lowering conditions. Adds nothing new.
Precise and correct for inspectors. It lists every (a)(1) trigger and the (b) devices, and correctly notes that (d)(4) has no empty-shaft exception, unlike (a)(1)(iv).
Accurate on exceptions, trainer requirements, breaks, restricted circumstances, validity periods, audit timing, deficiencies and effective dates. Leaving out retraining is acceptable for a summary.
Faithful to the section on military qualification, monitoring, the prohibited tasks, licensing and certification options, deficiency handling, evaluation, retraining and effective dates.

The checklist is accurate and fits the inspector level. It correctly covers the military scope, both certification options, audit requirements, documentation contents, language rules and the certification criteria.
Accurate to the section and pitched right for a trainee. It leaves out the (a)(3) documentation-at-site duty, but that is an employer task and the omission makes no statement wrong. Nothing is added.
Accurate and complete, including (a)(3). Paraphrases are faithful and nothing is added.
Accurate checklist for an inspector that covers all paragraphs. Quotes and definitions match the source and nothing is added.
Accurately covers (a)(1), both (a)(2) alternatives and (b), with correct citations. Notes that the definition is not given. Nothing is added.
Faithful to the source. The point that 'either/or' makes the two options alternatives is correct, and the 'in practice' line only restates (b).
Accurate checklist with correct citations. The wording difference between (a) and (b) and the stated limits on what the section covers are correct and add nothing new.
Correctly covers every paragraph (a)–(g) at trainee level, with accurate quotes and nothing added.
Correctly covers the operator duties in (c)(1)–(3), plus tag-out, crush/pinch points and training administration, with the other paragraphs noted briefly. Nothing is invented.
A correct role-by-role checklist with the right cross-references and conditions. Nothing is added.

Correct on the access demonstration and its exclusions, the platform exceptions, level and footing, 50% capacity, the 10° and 5x limits, 1/2 inch openings, 5x/10x rigging, 125% proof test for 5 minutes, 20 mph wind, 500 lb winch, power-line distances and one person per boatswain's chair. Pitched at trainee level.

Accurate operator-level summary. It covers the device-failure rule with its exact quote, controlled lowering, free-fall ban, proof-test steps, limits on other load lines and winches, travel and derrick limits, and power-line distances. No added content.

Accurate inspector checklist. It correctly separates (a)-(n) from (b)-(n), gets the lattice versus telescopic boom spotter rule right, and notes that only the pile-driving chair list includes (j). The marine-device conditions and tank-chair infeasibility rule are also correct.
Accurate and fits the trainee level. Explaining 'subpart' as the larger group of rules is a gloss, not a new duty. It covers all duties in (a) and (b).
Faithful to (a)(1)-(3) and (b)(1)-(2). The point that a competent person who is not also qualified needs qualified assistance follows logically from (b)(1).
Accurate checklist for inspectors. It correctly says the engineering trigger is the qualified person's determination and the duty is the employer's. It adds nothing beyond the text.
Accurate, trainee-level summary; omissions (latch design, para. (e)) don't make any statement wrong.
Calls the 250-lb cab roof rule a 'limit', making a minimum support-capacity design rule sound like a maximum load limit for workers. Otherwise accurate.
Accurate and thorough for an inspector: standards, prototype options, latch exception, guarding exceptions and the scope of para. (e) are all correct.

Gets the five routes, the engineer conditions, the 30 and 120 day limits, the rejection rule and the military exemption right. It leaves out the (b) rule that a rejection without written reasons can be treated as a refusal, but that's an option, not a central duty, and leaving it out makes nothing else wrong.
Matches every paragraph, including the 120-day start point and the case where reasons aren't given in writing. Nothing added.
Inspector checklist covers every condition correctly, with no added requirements.
Accurate trainee-level summary. The key numbers (1:500, 10 ft, 7 and 30 days, Nov 8 2011, last 2 wraps) are all correct, and it adds no new duties.
Faithful operator-level summary. Repair timelines, parts-order exceptions, the post-2011 conditions and the alternative measures are all correct.
Accurate inspector checklist. Cross-references, term substitutions, inspection items and timelines match the section.

The definition, the 6-guy minimum, the 110–125% hoist test, the 100–110% derrick test with its maximum-anticipated-load floor, the over-6,000 lb devices, the 30-day repair, power failure, boom securing and the daily guy check all match the source. Nothing is invented.

Load chart content and location, guy data, the device dates and thresholds, the 30-day and 7-day repair timelines, winch heads, boom securing and supervision are all accurate. Giving only the gin pole exception leaves out the stability rule but doesn't make anything wrong.
The welding standards, ASME B30.7 provisions, test percentages, documentation contents and retention, the 1926.1427 exclusion and the inspection items all match the source.
Accurate trainee summary. The scope, area control, devices, inspections, diver rules, Table M1–M3 numbers and the (n) list/trim and deck conditions all match the section. Nothing is invented.
Accurate operator summary. The exceptions, inspection cycles, documentation, diver rules, numbers, derating, list/trim limits, securing options and hull requirements are all faithful.

Accurate inspector checklist. The record references, retention and access, Table M1 derrick split, freeboard numbers, (n)(3) limits and the (n)(6) fallback to Options 1, 2 or 4 (rails left out) all match the section.

Correctly covers the permanent vs. not-permanent split, the §1910.179(b)(1) exception, the means-of-travel clause and both manufacture-date branches. Leaving out the specific lists is acceptable summarizing at trainee level.

The Part 1926 section list, the hoist/load definition carve-out, the pre/post September 19, 2001 rules and the 1910.147 substitution all match the source. The general description of the §1910.179 paragraphs is accurate.
Every citation, paragraph list, ASME section number, date and substitution matches the source exactly. Detail level suits an inspector.
Covers all four paragraphs correctly with the right citations and the correct date. It adds nothing and fits the trainee level.
Correct. It rightly says (b) removes only 1416(d)(3), and the inference about the rest of 1433 follows from "only". Nothing is invented.
Correct inspector-level framing. The cross-reference list is complete, and it rightly notes that the section does not define the term. Nothing is invented.

Correctly states the exclusions in (a), the free-fall exception and the live-boom date in (b), and the ASME B30.14-2004 requirement in (c). Summarizing the list is acceptable. Calling ASME a 'consensus standard' only describes it and adds no requirement.
Gives every exclusion, the date and all twelve ASME cross-references, including the paragraph limits in (c)(9)-(c)(12), accurately.

All section numbers, the date and the paragraph lists are accurate. It correctly notes that (f)(5), (k) and 14-1.7.5 are not listed. Leaving out the titles of the excluded sections is fine at inspector level.

Correctly covers who the section applies to, the cross-referenced rules, training, the personnel-hoisting ban, the load chart and electronic-capacity failure, and the two-block date. Nothing is invented.

Accurately summarizes the cross-references, assembly rules (including the engineer's written approval), procedures, accessibility, safety devices, anti two-block, training, the personnel ban and design. No errors.

The inspector checklist is faithful: it notes the qualified-rigger exception, both assembly routes, who develops which procedures (qualified person vs. engineer), the §1926.1416(d)(3) device and the date. Nothing is added.
Accurate plain-language summary of the general rule and all seven exceptions, with the right conditions; adds nothing.
Every exception is stated correctly with accurate citations; the hydraulic-cylinder condition is quoted exactly.
Complete and accurate citation checklist. The (b)(5) line is terse but in context it correctly conveys the condition for the exception.

Accurately summarizes the pin-removal rule, the exception, the A/D director's duty, both examples and the center-of-gravity rule; leaving out the reposition-and-repeat step is acceptable for a summary.

Faithful to the section, with the right citations and correct details on the assist crane, pin order and the tip test. Saying the lift 'cannot be repositioned' (the source says on the far side) is a minor simplification that still reads correctly in context.
Accurate (h)(6)(i)/(ii) citations, an exact quote of the exception, and correct sample measures. Keeping personnel clear before and during the raise matches the source.
Accurate plain-language overview of the four topic groups with correct citations. It correctly says the appendix sets no numeric limits and adds no duties.
Faithful, fairly complete summary of (a) through (d). Paraphrases such as 'reduced extension' for 'other than full' extension are accurate, and nothing is invented.
Accurate scope statement and cross-references (§§1926.1413-1416, 'every possible configuration', 'where applicable', Subpart CC shift inspection). It adds no requirements.
